campaigns_troop_and_creature_tables_summ.title: Domains at War - Campaigns Troop Tables

overview.rule: These tables summarize common demi-human, human, and beastman troops, including mercenaries and followers presented in ACKS core rules, Player’s Companion, and Domains at War: Campaigns.

notes.rule: When several equipment loadouts exist for a troop type, the default mercenary loadout is listed as A; variants are listed as B, C, and so on. Availability of variants is at the Judge’s discretion.
Cavalry characteristics separated by "/" distinguish rider and mount values for AC, HD, hp, number of attacks, and damage.
Battle Rating is listed per creature.

human_veteran_rule.rule: 25% of human units are veterans (1st level fighters).
Veterans have 1 HD, 5 hp, +1 morale, and +1 to damage rolls.

overview.rule: These tables summarize common demi-human, human, and beastman units.
Daily and weekly movement use the moving armies rules.
Monthly wage for a unit equals troop monthly wage multiplied by 120 for infantry or by 60 for cavalry or large creatures.
Supply cost is generally 60gp per week for infantry units and 240gp per week for cavalry units; units without quartermasters and carnivorous units pay more.
For all units except untrained conscripts and militia, assumed specialists are 1 quartermaster per unit and 1 armorer, 2 journeymen, and 4 apprentices per 240 troops.
Specialist cost assumptions above contribute 50gp per unit for a quartermaster and 160gp per 240 troops for armorers, journeymen, and apprentices.
Total monthly cost equals monthly wage cost plus monthly specialist cost plus four times weekly supply cost.
Battle Rating is per unit in these tables.

war_elephant_note.rule: For a unit of 5 veteran war elephants with 30 riders, monthly wages increase by 360gp because each of the 5 elephants is accompanied by 6 veteran troops.

overview.rule: These tables give Domains at War-specific characteristics for animals, constructs, fantastic creatures, oozes, undead, vermin, and other monsters. Standard creature characteristics are taken from the ACKS core monster listings unless modified here.

role.name: controlled
role.rule: Mindless creatures cannot be trained or led; they must be magically controlled.
Controlled troops can form a unit only if a lieutenant capable of controlling them is available.
Automatons, gargoyles, golems, and statues can be controlled by their creator or by special magic.
Mindless undead can be controlled by the spellcaster that animated them, by control undead magic, or by chaotic clerics that turn them with a D result.
Oozes can be controlled by charm monster or similar magic.

role.name: guards
role.rule: Guards are animal-intelligence creatures trained to attack designated targets and defend designated characters or locations.
Guards accompany handlers when requested and remain loyally in place when handlers are absent.
A unit of guards requires 1 creature handler specialist per 20 guard creatures.
Creature handlers for guard units do not fight and do not count as officers.
Guard training raises morale by 2 to a maximum of +2.
Guard training is equivalent to learning 7 tricks from an animal trainer.
Creatures lacking sufficient intelligence or temperament are usually trained as hunters instead of guards.

role.name: hunters
role.rule: Hunters are animal-intelligence creatures trained to accompany handlers on hunts, track designated targets, and kill them.
A unit of hunters requires 1 creature handler specialist per 6 hunter creatures.
Hunter training requires learning 2 tricks.
Hunters require constant monitoring and discipline to stay under control.

role.name: livestock
role.rule: Livestock are raised for food and receive only enough training to be safely handled.
Livestock are not useful in war except as supply.
Livestock cannot be formed into battlefield units except under exceptional circumstances or with magic, at Judge discretion.

role.name: mounts
role.rule: Mounts are creatures of animal or sentient intelligence trained to serve as steeds for irregular cavalry units.
Mount training counts as 5 tricks.
Even sentient rider-bearing creatures must be trained as mounts to communicate properly with riders and move while carrying them.
Creatures noted as Mount (S) are sentient and can also fight as troops.
Mounts without troops to ride them cannot be organized into units unless otherwise noted.

role.name: troops
role.rule: Troops are sentient creatures capable of fighting on the battlefield and are organized into units using standard rules.

role.name: war_mounts
role.rule: War mounts are animal-intelligence fighting steeds used with troops to form cavalry units.
War mount training counts as 8 tricks.
War mount training raises morale by 2 to a maximum of +2.
War mounts without riders can be organized into units as if they were guard creatures.

role.name: war_mount_troops
role.rule: War Mount/Troops are sentient creatures trained to fight both as troops and as war mounts.
Sentient creatures do not gain a morale increase from war mount training.
All sentient creatures capable of bearing riders are assumed to be trained in this manner because training cost is usually low relative to price.

role.name: workbeasts
role.rule: Workbeasts are trained to pull heavy loads or carry burdens.
Workbeasts cannot be formed into battlefield units except under exceptional circumstances or with magic, at Judge discretion.
Workbeast battle ratings are shown in parentheses.

normal_load_rules.rule: Normal load is the listed stone weight a creature can carry at full movement.
Most creatures can carry up to twice normal load at half movement.

Humanoids carry normal load at full movement, up to 1.5 times normal load at three-quarters movement, up to twice normal load at half movement, and up to four times normal load at one-quarter movement.

other_characteristics.rule: Price is the typical market purchase price in gp.
Animals, constructs, oozes, vermin, and other animal-intelligence creatures can usually be bought and sold as property in most realms.
Sentient creatures can be bought and sold as property only in chaotic realms where slavery is permitted; otherwise they must be hired as mercenaries.
Price varies by training; guards and war mounts often cost more.
Only free, sentient creatures normally hire themselves out as mercenaries.
Owned or enslaved sentient creatures can sometimes be rented from their owner; the listed wage then represents the rental fee.
A character pays no wage to creatures personally owned or enslaved.
If wages are 0, wage is low enough to be treated as included in supply cost.
Supply cost is per creature per week and reflects size and diet; carnivores cost more than herbivores, and larger creatures cost more than smaller creatures.
A normal man costs 0.5gp per week to supply for comparison.
Guard and hunter units require creature handlers: 1 handler per 20 guards or per 6 hunters.
Constructs, troops, mounts, and war mounts do not require creature handlers.
Constructs instead require lieutenants capable of controlling them.
Mounts are handled by their riders; troops use officers as normal.
Total monthly cost equals monthly wage cost plus monthly specialist cost plus four weeks of supply cost.
Owned or enslaved creatures cost less than listed total cost because no wage is paid.
Creature battle ratings in the roster are per creature; unit battle rating equals the sum of constituent creature battle ratings.
For comparison, a solitary human heavy infantryman has battle rating 0.017.
